questions.stem: Why does high humidity decrease the rate of transpiration?

options.text: Humid air is heavier and blocks the stomata
There is a smaller concentration gradient for water vapour between the leaf and the air
Water molecules in humid air are absorbed back into the leaf
Humidity causes stomata to close completely

questions.explanation: When humidity is high, there is already a lot of water vapour in the air outside the leaf. This reduces the concentration gradient between the moist air spaces inside the leaf and the outside, so water vapour diffuses out more slowly.
